interpretation: Each cell has16 game seeds; do not pool policy-seed repeats into48 independent environments or new builder diversity. All64 builder3-tuples exactly match after ignoring only the two strategy.seed metadata fields.

Random-auto creates rewardRandom from strategy.seed without consuming World RNG. Reusing one fixed policy seed across16 game seeds reuses the reward-choice index stream. This is policy sensitivity, not independent random decisions per environment.

For all16 game seeds in both layouts, policy1 and97 select first-offer slot1 (zero-based); policy17 selects slot2. Guided drawCards reserves initial first2 slots for foundation upgrades (or later invested family); third slot is an alternative.

Policy17 narrow has0/16 first clears and wins (Wilson0–19.36%); wide2/16 first clears and1/16 win. Its narrow first picks are14 non-foundation and2 foundation cards. Observations are consistent with shared slot stream plus ordered offers and weak starts; no isolated counterfactual proves the first card caused death, no software defect proven.

Builder800→2400 win rates are75→50% for auto and81.25→62.5% for active, with first clear100% in both layouts. Auto25pp layout gap exceeds the investigation reference; allpaired layout outcomes preserved. Small16seed samples and deterministic3repeat controls do not strengthen precision.
Random800→2400 rates vary62.5→25%,0→6.25%,56.25→37.5% across policy1/17/97. Single policy success rates cannot be generalized to humans or arbitrary reward behavior.
All41 original warnings retained, including18small_sample/10stage_drop/6build_concentration/3target_gain/4layout_gap. Repeated deterministic builder warnings are not independent confirmations.
All288 resolve as159 campaign victories and129 normal deaths; no budget/error/cancel. Allwinner tails and zero-inclusive actualHP+shield distributions remain in stable audit.
No new simulations, tuning, policy changes, thresholds or replacement seeds; this annex interprets the unchanged completed matrix. Final adoption remains root full-evidence judgment.
